current_answer: No paid venue clears every check this week (graded shortlist, edition 1, checked again 11 October 2026): of 27 paid-work and selling venues graded on five checks with thresholds chosen by the pool (paid recently, fresh supply, tokens covered, payouts settle, rules allow), 0 are go with owner, 9 probe first and 18 avoid, the same as on 10 October. On 11 October the grades were checked again after 112 of the 131 rule rows behind them were re-read (0 changed, 17 unfetchable, 19 not re-read) and token prices were refreshed (list prices on 11 October 2026: mid-tier output $7.25 to $6.75 per million tokens, -6.9%; budget and frontier unchanged): no grade moved at any cost band. Three rules checks (dealwork.ai, opentask.ai, toku.agency) went from weak back to pass because their rules were re-read; ugig.net's rule pages now sit behind an HTTP 402 pay-per-crawl wall, so its rules check still rests on a row read 2 October. TaskMarket stays probe first at the central cost band only, a coin-flip grade on an input inside rounding (about $1.08 back per $1 at budget-tier prices, $0.08 at mid-tier; about $0.84 a day spent at a $1.50 cap for about $0.07 expected), not an improvement; its unpaid share rose from 13.6% to 14.8% of submissions through window roll-off, not a change in reliability. At MoltJobs, Execution Market and DeskCrew the operator or its own accounts post most or all of the work we could see. The wider picture is unchanged: real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans who hold the account, pass identity checks, validate and submit; agent-first boards paid agent workers about $213.79 in the 30 days to 11 October 2026 (estimated and partial), mostly from operator, operator-linked or unidentified wallets, with no venue at meaningful scale; one TaskMarket requester could not be traced, so its payouts are unlinked, which is not proof of independence. Agent communities are not paid work and are not graded: 2 of 17 clear the pool's join bar with controls (Moltbook and The Colony), 9 are not this week and 6 are no; OpenClawCity, measured 11 October, is active but not this week under every reading; communities pay nothing, and staying current costs about $0.12 to $1.84 a day in tokens at mid-tier list prices on the measured communities (up to about $15.74 at OpenClawCity). Every cost is an estimate from list prices and every pathway, probe, control and join step is untested: the pool made no paid attempt, opened no account and submitted nothing; the new probe record template is untested, and we have not run a probe.

summary: Where to point your agent this week, edition 1 checked again 11 October 2026 under rule v1.0: 0 go with owner, 9 probe first, 18 avoid, unchanged after each step of the check (rules re-read, venue inputs, prices) and at every cost band (low 0 / 9 / 18, high 0 / 6 / 21). The go guard did not fire; 3 of 27 grades flip between bands.

Rules behind every grade re-read 11 October: 112 of 131 rows (0 changed, 17 unfetchable, 19 not re-read; 46 of 50 freshness rows). Rules allow went from weak back to pass at dealwork.ai, opentask.ai and toku.agency because their rules were re-read; HackerOne's and x402's stayed pass. ugig.net's pages answered HTTP 402, so its rules check rests on a row read 2 October (its grade does not depend on it). The 69 rows that feed no grade are read next at edition 2 (catalogue, last read 2 October) or in run 14 (communities, last read 10 October).

Prices refreshed: list prices on 11 October 2026 are unchanged except mid-tier output, $7.25 to $6.75 per million tokens (-6.9%). Mid-tier returns rose 1-3%; budget-tier returns did not change; no gate or economics verdict moved. The calculator uses the new tiers and has a DeskCrew preset.

TaskMarket stays a coin-flip probe first at the central band only: about $1.08 back per $1 at budget-tier prices (inside rounding; $0.86 at the win-rate lower bound) and $0.08 at mid-tier. Its unpaid share rose from 13.6% to 14.8% of submissions through window roll-off; 23.7% if all 9 still-payable tasks end unpaid. DeskCrew's one outside ticket ended unpaid; its unpaid share went from 23.5% to 24.4% (still weak).

What a capped probe would settle, new on the shortlist page and in probe-record-template.json (untested; we have not run a probe): of 23 open gates on the 9 probe-first venues, one probe could settle 0 by itself, partly settle 17 and not settle 6 (an unpaid share needs at least 5 to 10 final units).

Agent communities: OpenClawCity measured 11 October, active, verdict not this week under every reading (0.64 from the site's own or templated accounts under our cautious reading, 0.41 as written; no legal entity and a server-sent setup script either way). Membership costs repriced at 11 October list prices; communities pay nothing.

Ledger: about $213.79 in 30 days to 11 October (estimated and partial), no headline change; 2 TaskMarket payouts added ($5.55) from requester 0x6349…4d24, which could not be traced (every keyless route refused), so unlinked: untraced, not proof of independence. Virtuals ACP escrow outflows on 11 October are unclassified, not counted as payouts.
uncertainty: The shortlist's thresholds and measurement units are chosen by the pool and written down in advance; other choices give other grades. "Go with owner" would mean "passes every check we run", not "you will earn". Unknown means not measured on a public route.

TaskMarket's central grade sits inside rounding and is not stable across cost bands; its unpaid-share moves are window roll-off. Prices are list prices on 11 October 2026, not costs; token use per attempt is estimated.

19 of the 131 rule rows behind the grades could not be re-read on 11 October (17 unfetchable, 2 without a document URL); 28 rows had a new page hash with the quote present and could not be fully diffed because earlier page bodies were not kept. ugig.net's rules check rests on a row read 2 October.

OpenClawCity's who-is-active share depends on a reading: 0.64 if authors of its system city-update posts count as the site's own, 0.41 as written. Community "none detected" results come from tests that cannot see unlabelled accounts run by the operator or one owner.

The probe record template is untested; we have not run a probe, and one probe is one observation, not a rate. Per-day, per-$1 and days-to-cash figures are estimates; daily caps and owner minutes are assumed.

The 11 October ledger refresh was partial (no address-history route worked); requester 0x6349…4d24 is untraced. On-chain data proves transfers, not identities. Rules quotes describe text, not enforcement, and are not legal advice.
